buttonLabel: "Explore tours through the Uco Valley"
lead: >-
  The Uco Valley in Argentina's Mendoza Province features in itineraries where wineries are a destination in their own right. Some tours devote an entire day to the valley, with several tastings; others combine this wine region with Buenos Aires, Patagonia, Iguazú, or Chile. Discover how the actual Ada Tours programs differ, how much time to allow for vineyards at the foot of the Andes, and how to choose by experience rather than simply the number of days.
---

## Tours through the Uco Valley: choosing a wine journey

If discovering Argentina's wineries is the main purpose of your trip, consider itineraries that dedicate a full day to the [Uco Valley](/argentina/place/uco-valley/). Vineyards stretch across the Andean foothills, and tastings can be combined with visits to production facilities and explanations of how wines are aged. In Ada Tours itineraries, the valley appears both as the main culinary highlight and as a stop on a larger continental journey.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through the Uco Valley. Compare them by **the number and content of wine-focused days**, the geography of other stops, guiding arrangements, and transfers. A longer Argentina tour does not necessarily offer more tastings than a shorter, specialized program.

[Mendoza](/argentina/place/mendoza/) is the natural departure point for the wine districts. It combines well with [Luján de Cuyo](/argentina/place/lujan-de-cuyo/), while travelers interested in a dedicated experience can choose a [guided Uco Valley winery and tasting excursion](/argentina/uco-valley/uco-valley-winery-tasting/).

## Which tours include the Uco Valley?

### 9 days: wineries in Argentina and Chile

The [9-day tour of Argentina and Chile](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/) begins in Buenos Aires, continues to Mendoza, and finishes in Santiago. A separate day is devoted to the Uco Valley: accompanied by a specialist guide, the program includes **visits to 3 wineries**. In Chile, travelers visit the Concha y Toro winery as well as Valparaíso and Viña del Mar.

This option suits travelers who want to spend time among the vineyards and compare the winemaking traditions of 2 countries. The other days add the culture and tango of Buenos Aires and an introduction to the Chilean coast. Before choosing, check the tastings included and the conditions for each visit directly in the tour description.

### 12 days: Uco Valley, glaciers, and Iguazú

The [route through Buenos Aires, Mendoza, El Calafate, and Iguazú](/argentina/tour/argentina-buenos-aires-mendoza-el-calafate-iguazu/) devotes its Uco Valley wine day to visits to 3 wineries with a guide specializing in wine. The scenery then changes dramatically: [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) and Iguazú Falls provide completely different experiences.

Choose this itinerary if you want a substantial wine excursion while devoting most of your vacation to several celebrated regions of Argentina. Unlike the 9-day itinerary with Chile, this program includes more natural attractions, with winemaking occupying a limited portion of the journey.

### 13 days: vineyards, the Andes, and ancient landscapes

The [Argentina journey through Mendoza and San Juan](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/) combines Uco Valley wineries with Andean roads, the Aconcagua area, geological parks, and Patagonia's Atlantic coastline. The valley program includes **3 wineries**, where the guide explains grape cultivation, winemaking, and maturation.

The defining feature of this itinerary is its focus on geography and the history of the Earth. After the vineyards, you will see [Aconcagua](/argentina/place/aconcagua/) and other mountain landscapes, followed later by natural areas near [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/). It is a good combination for travelers equally interested in wine and nature.

### 15 days: a private itinerary with wine-focused days

The [15-day grand tour of Argentina](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/) links Buenos Aires, both sides of Iguazú Falls, northern Argentina, Mendoza, and Patagonia. Its wine program includes distinct outings: tastings in Luján de Cuyo, followed by a separate visit to boutique wineries in the Uco Valley with a Russian-speaking guide.

Consider this private itinerary if you want a substantial cultural and nature program throughout the journey, with wineries as a meaningful part of it. Separate days in 2 wine-growing districts make it possible to compare the regions without devoting the entire vacation to vineyards.

### 26 days: wine regions within an extensive expedition

The [26-day overview of Argentina and neighboring countries](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) includes northwestern Argentina, Mendoza, Patagonia, and other regions. Around Mendoza, separate days are allocated to Luján de Cuyo and the Uco Valley. In the latter, the program includes visits to **2 wineries**.

The longer duration serves the broad geographic scope, not wine tourism alone. This option suits travelers who have time for an extended journey, want to see different natural zones, and still wish to enjoy wine tastings.

## Quick itinerary comparison

| Travel goal | Suitable tour |
|---|---|
| Wines of Argentina and Chile | [9 days, 2 countries](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/) |
| Wine, glaciers, and waterfalls | [12 days in Argentina](/argentina/tour/argentina-buenos-aires-mendoza-el-calafate-iguazu/) |
| Wine, Andes, and geology | [13-day itinerary](/argentina/tour/argentina-prehistoric-journey/) |
| Extended private journey | [15 days from Iguazú to Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/) |
| The broadest geographical coverage | [26-day tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) |

When comparing prices, consider accommodation type, group size, flights, and included services: the prices of a short wine tour and a major private journey reflect very different travel arrangements. The detailed terms are provided on the individual tour pages.

## How much time should you spend in the Uco Valley?

**One full day** is enough for a substantial visit to several wineries if your route has already brought you to Mendoza. This is the format used in several current Ada Tours programs. If you prefer leisurely tastings, gastronomic lunches, and time among the vines, consider staying longer in the region or arranging accommodation nearby. Any such extension must be agreed for the specific itinerary; it is not automatically included in every tour through the Uco Valley.

Winery visits require advance planning. Schedules, available tasting sets, and opportunities to have lunch at a winery vary. A proper wine-focused day includes not only driving through scenic valleys but also reserved time at the estates. After tasting wine, traveling with a driver is more sensible than driving yourself.

## When to visit for wine and Andean scenery

The Uco Valley lies at the foot of the Andes, in a dry wine-growing area of Mendoza Province. **The grape harvest generally takes place toward the end of the Southern Hemisphere summer and the beginning of autumn**, usually in February–March, although timing varies with grape variety and weather. This is an interesting time to learn about winemaking. Vineyard colors change in autumn; snow-covered peaks may be visible in winter. Throughout the year, visits differ in weather and in the activities offered by wineries.

Argentina's official tourism portal recommends booking winery visits in advance. When planning, consider driving times between estates and the temperature difference between a sunny day and a cool evening. For a wider range of culinary destinations, see [Argentina's wine and food tours](/interests/food-and-wine/tours/argentina/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Can I visit the Uco Valley without a multi-day wine tour?

Yes. You can conveniently add a full wine-focused day to a stay in Mendoza. Ada Tours offers a separate [Uco Valley winery excursion](/argentina/uco-valley/uco-valley-winery-tasting/) with a Russian-speaking guide and tasting. Its terms differ from those of winery visits included in multi-day programs.

### Do all tours visit 3 wineries?

No. The 9-, 12-, and 13-day programs confirm visits to 3 estates, while the 26-day program visits 2. Other tours differ in the number and duration of winery visits. Check your selected itinerary rather than assuming the same number of visits as another tour.

### What is the difference between the Uco Valley and Luján de Cuyo?

These are separate wine-growing districts of Mendoza Province. The Uco Valley is particularly associated with foothill vineyards and high-altitude wines; [Luján de Cuyo](/argentina/place/lujan-de-cuyo/) is also renowned for its wineries and Malbec. Some Ada Tours itineraries visit both districts on separate days.

### Is it necessary to combine the Uco Valley with Chile?

No. There are Argentina-only and multi-country journeys. Chile features in the [9-day wine tour](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-mendoza-wine-9-days/), but the [12-day program with Patagonia and Iguazú](/argentina/tour/argentina-buenos-aires-mendoza-el-calafate-iguazu/) focuses on Argentine regions.

### How should I choose if wine is my main interest?

Compare the number of wine days and tastings, whether a guide accompanies you, and the time spent traveling between sites. Start with the 9-day program and compare it with the 15-day option, where wine regions are part of a longer private tour. Choose according to the experiences that matter most to you.

buttonLabel: "Explore Uquía and the Arquebusier Angels"
lead: >-
  Uquía is a small settlement in Argentina's Quebrada de Humahuaca. The main reason to stop here is the Church of San Francisco de Paula, known for its colonial architecture and paintings of the Arquebusier Angels. A visit introduces the religious art of the Andes and reveals how local artists reinterpreted European imagery.
---

## Uquía: San Francisco de Paula Church and the Arquebusier Angels

**Uquía is a small settlement in Jujuy Province worth including in a cultural journey through the [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/).** Against dry mountain slopes, its light-colored church and freestanding bell tower stand out. Behind the modest exterior is an important collection of colonial religious paintings.

The village is a convenient stop between [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/) and the [town of Humahuaca](/argentina/place/humahuaca/). Its main attractions are the church, the history of the local community, and the artistic dialogue between different traditions. On a general tour of the valley, Uquía takes less time than a major archaeological site, but it merits its own explanation.

## What is known about the old church?

The church's full historical name is the **Chapel of the Holy Cross and San Francisco de Paula**. Argentina's official register of monuments dates the earliest documentary evidence of construction to **1691**. The building retains features typical of colonial churches in the northern Andes.

This single-nave church has a simple pitched roof, an atrium, and a freestanding bell tower. Its walls are built of adobe, traditional sun-dried bricks; local building techniques reflected the available materials and valley climate. Inside is an old carved altar. The church is protected as a National Historic Monument of Argentina.

The simple exterior contrasts strikingly with the richness within. Yet the church is worth visiting for more than its architecture: its art collection offers insight into how Baroque painting spread through the Andes.

## Who are the Arquebusier Angels?

Uquía's most recognizable artistic subject is the **Arquebusier Angels**: heavenly figures wearing elaborate 17th-century clothing and carrying early firearms called arquebuses. This unusual blend of angelic figures, military attributes, and rich fabrics belongs to the tradition of colonial Andean art.

The surviving series is associated with the **Cusco school of painting**. Provincial heritage-preservation materials refer to **9 paintings** in the series. Their importance lies in how European religious iconography acquired its own form within Andean cultural traditions.

Distinguish the historical importance of the artworks from whether they are currently on display. The paintings have undergone conservation and restoration procedures, and viewing arrangements may change. Before arriving, confirm whether the church is open and whether visitors can see the works on your chosen day.

## Why Uquía matters to the valley's cultural landscape

The Quebrada de Humahuaca is a UNESCO World Heritage Site recognized as a historic corridor of exchange and settlement. Traces of pre-Columbian communities, colonial churches, and small living communities stand close to one another.

In [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/), travelers primarily encounter archaeology at the ancient Pucará settlement. In [Uquía](/argentina/place/uquia/), the central theme is colonial religious culture. [Humahuaca](/argentina/place/humahuaca/) adds historic streets, civic buildings, and monuments. Together, these stops illustrate different periods of the region's development without reducing its history to a single era.

## How to plan a stop in Uquía

For a short visit, focus on the church, its surrounding historic setting, and the small settlement itself. If you want to study the paintings closely, check access hours and the possibility of a guided visit in advance. This is an active place of worship; during services and ceremonies, visitor arrangements may differ.

On exposed stretches of the valley, expect strong sun, dry air, and the altitude of northern Argentina. Comfortable footwear, drinking water, and a hat are useful even for a short stop. With limited time, it is better to divide an excursion among 2–3 meaningful sites than to stop at every landmark along the road.

## Uquía on Ada Tours itineraries

On our ["Amazing Salta" tour](/argentina/tour/amazing-salta/), Uquía is visited during a journey through Purmamarca, Tilcara, and the Humahuaca Gorge. On the [grand tour of Argentina](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/), Uquía is part of a cultural stage with other landmarks in the country's northwest. History enthusiasts can also explore our [culture and history journeys](/interests/culture-and-history/).

When comparing programs, check whether Uquía is a proper stop, whether entry to the church is included, whether there is time to see the paintings, and whether a guide accompanies the visit. Merely listing the village in an itinerary does not mean church admission is included.

## Frequently asked questions about Uquía

### How is Uquía different from Tilcara?

Uquía is chiefly known for its colonial church and paintings. [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/) is notable for the Pucará archaeological complex. Together, they reveal different eras of the valley's history.

### Does Uquía's church really have paintings of angels carrying guns?

Yes. The Arquebusier Angels are a distinctive theme in colonial Andean Baroque art. Nine paintings survive in the church's historic collection; check whether they can actually be viewed before visiting.

### Should I devote an entire day to Uquía?

Not usually for the church alone. Uquía makes a rewarding stop between Tilcara and Humahuaca, while a full day can cover several places in the gorge.

### Can I visit the church without a guide?

Visiting arrangements depend on the church's schedule and protection of the artworks. A guide can explain the painting tradition and its 17th-century context, but access inside and any guiding arrangement should be confirmed against the program.

## Tours through Uquía: colonial art along the Humahuaca Gorge

[Uquía](/argentina/place/uquia/) is a stop for travelers who want to discover the cultural heritage of Andean settlements. It lies in the [Quebrada de Humahuaca](/argentina/place/quebrada-de-humahuaca/), a mountain corridor in northwestern Argentina's Jujuy Province. The old Church of San Francisco de Paula houses the famous Arquebusier Angels collection: colonial religious images portraying angels in military dress with firearms.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} incorporating Uquía into their main itineraries. **These are journeys through several settlements in the gorge, not multi-day stays in Uquía itself.** The main choice is between a short program focused on the northwest and a longer trip spanning different regions of Argentina. The overall duration, other stops, and travel arrangements determine which tour will suit you best.

## Which itineraries pass through Uquía?

### 5 days: Salta, mountain roads, and northern settlements

The [5-day "Amazing Salta" tour](/argentina/tour/amazing-salta/) is the most compact option shown here. It includes [Salta](/argentina/place/salta/), the Cafayate wine district, high-altitude scenery, [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/), [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/), Uquía, and [Salinas Grandes](/argentina/place/salinas-grandes/).

This format devotes almost the entire trip to the country's northwest. Uquía becomes part of a coherent exploration of Humahuaca Gorge: the church, traditional settlements, multicolored hillsides, and cultural landmarks fall along a single route. Choose this tour if you are especially interested in Jujuy Province and northern Argentina, leaving the southern glaciers and Iguazú for another trip.

### 15 days: northern Argentina, Mendoza, Patagonia, and Iguazú

The [15-day overview tour of Argentina](/argentina/tour/argentina-patagonia-highlights-2024/) adds Buenos Aires, the Mendoza wine regions, Patagonia, and Iguazú Falls to the northern settlements. On the northern leg, after Purmamarca and Tilcara, travelers visit Uquía and its church before continuing toward the [town of Humahuaca](/argentina/place/humahuaca/).

Here Uquía is one cultural episode in a larger sightseeing program. It is a good choice if you want to see Argentina's main contrasts in one vacation: southern glaciers, subtropical waterfalls, vineyards, and dry Andean gorges. The northwest receives less time than on the dedicated 5-day journey.

### 15 days: a private journey from Iguazú to Patagonia

On the [private 15-day Argentina journey](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/), a day in the north is spent with a Russian-speaking guide. The day's stops include the [Hill of Seven Colors near Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/), Tilcara, Uquía, Humahuaca, and Inca Cueva. The program then continues through Mendoza with wine tastings and El Calafate with Perito Moreno Glacier.

This tour differs through its confirmed guiding arrangements on the gorge visit and its private travel format. Consider the pace of the day when choosing: several places are scheduled, so each stop has a defined amount of time. If exploring the church interior thoroughly or spending longer in Uquía is a priority, discuss this when planning your journey.

### 26 days: extended itineraries including Uquía

The [26-day overview of Argentina and neighboring countries](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) combines the country's northwest with Mendoza, Bariloche, Ushuaia, glaciers, and other regions. Here Uquía forms part of a lengthy sequence of northern settlements alongside Purmamarca, Tilcara, and Humahuaca.

Another extended option is ["Chile and Argentina VIP"](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-vip/), in which Uquía also features in a broad itinerary covering Patagonia and northern Argentina. Such tours are selected for their extensive geography; seeing Uquía in the list of places does not mean there is a long standalone village excursion. Compare the program for the relevant day, the transport, and the services already included on the specific tour page.

## Choosing a tour based on your main goal

| What matters | Suitable option |
|---|---|
| Northern Argentina on a short trip | [5 days in Salta and Jujuy](/argentina/tour/amazing-salta/) |
| Several natural regions of the country | [15-day overview](/argentina/tour/argentina-patagonia-highlights-2024/) |
| A private program and guiding | [15-day Grand Tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-grand-tour-15-days/) |
| Extensive itinerary across Argentina | [26-day journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) |
| Chile and Argentina in a single trip | [Extensive VIP itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-vip/) |

All these options share one cultural stop but follow different travel patterns. Visiting Uquía itself does not require a 15–26-day vacation. Choose a longer tour for the other regions and experiences, rather than expecting it to provide extra time in a small village.

## What exactly should you see in Uquía?

The main landmark is the **Church of San Francisco de Paula**. Its historic building belongs to Jujuy's colonial heritage, with whitewashed walls, a simple form, and a freestanding bell tower. The church is protected as a National Historic Monument of Argentina. The best-known works in its collection are 17th-century paintings of arquebusier angels, associated with the artistic traditions of the colonial Andes.

The subject is unusual: the angels wear clothing reminiscent of military uniforms and carry arquebuses. These works illustrate how European religious iconography changed within Andean art. For this visit, time spent inside the church and listening to the guide's explanations matters more than the number of village buildings you can walk past.

The Quebrada de Humahuaca is on the UNESCO World Heritage List as an **integrated cultural landscape and historic route**. This designation applies to the gorge as a whole, not as an individual award to every church. The site tells of thousands of years of movement of people, goods, and cultural traditions between the high Andes and the plains. It therefore makes sense to explore Uquía with other places in the gorge, rather than as an isolated stop.

## How an itinerary day is arranged

A trip passing through Uquía commonly combines several stops: [Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) and the Hill of Seven Colors, [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/) and its archaeological heritage, Uquía and the church, and [Humahuaca](/argentina/place/humahuaca/) with its historic streets. Some tours also include [Salinas Grandes](/argentina/place/salinas-grandes/) and other natural stops.

The settlement lies along National Route No. 9, making it a convenient stop on a journey through the gorge. **Access to the church interior must be confirmed separately**: visiting hours depend on actual opening arrangements, religious services, and local circumstances. A scheduled stop does not guarantee that the church will be open at any given moment.

Northwestern Argentina is at a considerably higher altitude than Buenos Aires. Even on a sunny day, mornings and evenings in the mountains can be cool, the sun intense, and temperature swings pronounced. Bring drinking water, sun protection, and clothes that can be layered easily. On long driving days, the most important consideration is allocating enough time between stops.

## How is Uquía different from nearby places?

[Purmamarca](/argentina/place/purmamarca/) is particularly famous for its colorful slopes and view of the Hill of Seven Colors. [Tilcara](/argentina/place/tilcara/) is known for archaeology and settlement history. In [Humahuaca](/argentina/place/humahuaca/), the focus shifts toward urban heritage and the surrounding valley. **Uquía stands out above all for its colonial church and paintings.**

If you are interested in architecture, religious art, and the history of the northern Andes, this stop has special value. If natural landscapes are your main motivation, Uquía complements the colorful mountains and salt flats but does not replace them. For other historic itineraries, explore current [culture and history tours in Argentina](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/argentina/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Is there a dedicated multi-day tour only to Uquía?

In the current Ada Tours catalog, Uquía appears as part of routes through northwestern Argentina. For an independent visit to the village, it is usually enough to include a stop on a day exploring Humahuaca Gorge. The main multi-day programs cover several places.

### Can I visit Uquía on a trip from Salta?

Yes. The [5-day "Amazing Salta" itinerary](/argentina/tour/amazing-salta/) includes Uquía alongside northern settlements, salt flats, and the Cafayate wine region. It is a convenient introduction to the area without traveling to Patagonia.

### Why is the Church of San Francisco de Paula famous?

For its historic architecture and the Arquebusier Angels collection. It is a monument to colonial Andean art, showing religious figures with military attributes. Whether the collection can be seen inside the church depends on visiting arrangements.

### Is Uquía part of a UNESCO site?

It lies within Quebrada de Humahuaca, recognized by UNESCO as a cultural landscape and historic route. The designation belongs to the entire gorge. Together, settlements, chapels, roads, and archaeological sites reveal its historical importance.

### Which tour is best for a first visit to northwestern Argentina?

If your main goal is to see Uquía, Tilcara, Purmamarca, and the local landscapes, start with the [5-day program](/argentina/tour/amazing-salta/). Choose one of the 15- or 26-day tours if you also want to visit Iguazú, Mendoza, Patagonia, or Chile.

  Ushuaia, on Tierra del Fuego, is a base for trips along the Beagle Channel, visits to the national park, and exploration of mountain landscapes. Many Antarctic expeditions also depart from here. ## Ushuaia: the Beagle Channel, Tierra del Fuego, and the gateway to Antarctica

**Ushuaia lets you experience southern Argentina's landscapes from both land and water.** The city stands on the Tierra del Fuego archipelago, on the shores of the Beagle Channel, surrounded by mountains. Catamarans and expedition vessels leave its port, while forest and coastal trails begin in the nearby national park.

The city is often called the "End of the World." For travelers, the more useful question is what you want to do: watch seabirds, walk through subantarctic forest, see mountain lakes, or begin an [Antarctic expedition](/antarctica/).

## The Beagle Channel: what can you see from the water?

Boat excursions from Ushuaia's port sail along the Beagle Channel. Itineraries may include islands, colonies of sea lions, cormorants, and other marine species. One well-known landmark is Les Éclaireurs Lighthouse, surrounded by coastal rocks.

Argentina's tourism portal describes catamaran trips, but actual stops and landings vary by operator. **A short Beagle Channel excursion is not an Antarctic cruise** and does not guarantee penguin sightings on every island.

| Format | Main focus |
|---|---|
| Beagle Channel catamaran | Marine landscapes and birds |
| National park | Forest and coastal trails |
| Mountain hike | Lakes and more challenging terrain |
| Antarctic ship | Multi-day expedition |

Strong winds, cold, and rough seas are possible even in summer. Schedules depend on the weather and crew decisions.

## Tierra del Fuego National Park

**Parque Nacional Tierra del Fuego** is near the city. It combines forests, peat bogs, lakes, and the shores of the Beagle Channel. The Argentine park authority publishes separate routes of varying difficulty, from short walks to long trails with elevation gain.

Well-known visitor areas include Lapataia Bay and coastal trails. Parts of the park also contain the road leading to the end of National Route No. 3. Travelers can experience the transition from forest to cold marine shores.

Visitors cannot roam freely through all parts of the park: designated trails, environmental protection rules, and seasonal restrictions apply. Check which trails are open, road access, and clothing requirements before visiting.

## The End of the World Train and the city's history

Ushuaia is historically associated with its former prison and the settlement of Tierra del Fuego. The End of the World Train is a popular visitor experience that introduces part of this history and the landscapes outside the city. A separate museum exhibition in the city explores the region's history.

It is important to distinguish evocative names from actual products. The historic train is a standalone excursion with its own ticket, while visiting the museum is another activity. Their appearance on a general list of attractions does not mean they are automatically included in every itinerary.

## Antarctica begins with logistics

Ushuaia is one of the main departure ports for Antarctic expeditions. Simply stopping in Ushuaia, however, does not mean visiting the Antarctic Peninsula. These are journeys of different lengths and costs, requiring separate planning and a ship reservation.

We offer dedicated [Antarctic expeditions](/antarctica/tour/) and [Tierra del Fuego journeys](/multi-country/tour/tierra-del-fuego-fjords/). When arranging a flight to the departure port, allow extra time before boarding the vessel to account for possible route and weather changes.

## Combining Ushuaia with other Argentine cities

Ushuaia is often combined with [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/) and [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). The [12-day Argentina trip with Patagonia and Iguazú](/multi-country/tour/argentina-buenos-aires-el-calafate-ushuaia-iguazu-12-days/) takes in these destinations, but requires domestic flights between them.

If Tierra del Fuego's nature trails are your main interest, we recommend allowing at least **two sightseeing days**: one for the park, another for the Beagle Channel or a more active route. This is a planning recommendation, not a confirmed duration of a particular tour.

## Weather and safety

Tierra del Fuego is known for changeable, windy weather. Walks require warm layers, waterproof outerwear, and sturdy footwear. Mountain paths may feature ice, mud, and stretches of peat bog; in winter, some routes close or require specialized equipment.

Do not start long hikes without knowing current conditions, and follow crew instructions on any marine excursion. Even a short outing here can be far more dependent on the weather than a city sightseeing tour.

## Frequently asked questions about Ushuaia

### Is Ushuaia in Antarctica?

No. Ushuaia is an Argentine city on Tierra del Fuego. Many Antarctic expeditions depart from its port.

### Where is the best place to see sea lions and birds?

On boat routes through the Beagle Channel, although actual sightings and stops depend on the chosen excursion.

### Can I visit the national park without difficult trekking?

Yes. The park has trails of varying difficulty, including short walks. Check access to particular routes against current park regulations.

## Tours through Ushuaia: what to choose and how many days to spend in Tierra del Fuego

[Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) stands on the [Beagle Channel](/argentina/place/beagle-channel/), between the sea and the mountains of Tierra del Fuego. Excursions to [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/), visits to lakes, boat trips, and cruises depart from here. Our catalog includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Ushuaia on their main itineraries.

**The first thing to check is Ushuaia's role in the program.** A tour mentioning the city in its title might include a substantial stay with excursions, a brief embarkation on a ship, or disembarkation after an expedition. These are different kinds of travel despite the shared point on the map. The second criterion is how much time is dedicated specifically to Tierra del Fuego rather than all of Patagonia, Argentina, or Antarctica.

For travelers who want to explore the city and surrounding area in depth, overland itineraries with overnight stays in Ushuaia work well. Those who enjoy sailing among fjords may prefer marine programs ending here. Antarctic journeys are chosen for the expedition itself, with Ushuaia serving as the departure port.

## Overland journeys: Ushuaia, glaciers, and neighboring countries

### 12 days: "Ice, Sun and the End of the World"

The [private 12-day tour of Argentina and Brazil](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/) links Buenos Aires, glaciers around [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), Ushuaia, Iguazú Falls, and Rio de Janeiro. **The itinerary includes 2 nights in Ushuaia** and a visit to Tierra del Fuego National Park.

It suits travelers who want to experience the cold southern shores and Patagonian ice before switching to subtropical waterfalls and Brazil's coast. The program, however, is spread across several distant regions, leaving little free time for a detailed exploration of Tierra del Fuego. On this tour's product page, group excursions in Ushuaia are listed with an English-speaking guide; private Russian-language guiding is offered for an additional fee and is not automatically included.

### 13 days: Argentina, Chile, and Patagonia

On the [13-day tour of Argentine and Chilean Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/), the journey begins in Buenos Aires before moving to Tierra del Fuego. Around Ushuaia, a **road trip to the lakes** and a visit to the national park are scheduled, after which the itinerary continues to El Calafate, El Chaltén, and Chile's Torres del Paine.

This journey better suits the goal of experiencing Patagonia's diverse landscapes: coast, forests, mountain lakes, [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), hiking trails, and Chilean national parks. Compared with the 12-day tour, the main difference is the focus on the southern landscapes of Argentina and Chile instead of continuing to Iguazú and Rio.

### 16 days: wildlife, the Beagle Channel, and lakes

The [16-day Argentina journey](/argentina/tour/explore-argentina-16-days/) travels along the Atlantic coast through [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/), then on to Ushuaia, El Calafate, and Iguazú. In Ushuaia, the program includes separate experiences in the national park, **a boat trip on the Beagle Channel**, and an off-road excursion to [Lake Fagnano](/argentina/place/lake-fagnano/) and [Lake Escondido](/argentina/place/lake-escondido-tierra-del-fuego/).

Unlike a short port call, this allows travelers to experience several sides of Tierra del Fuego: coastal wildlife, protected forests, and mountain lakes. It is a good choice for those who want to spend more time in Ushuaia while also seeing Patagonia's marine wildlife, glaciers, and waterfalls.

### 26 days: an extensive journey across two countries

The ["Chile and Argentina VIP" itinerary](/multi-country/tour/chile-argentina-vip/) includes Ushuaia among many stops at the southern end of the continent, then continues through other regions of Patagonia and northern Argentina. This tour suits travelers who want to cover many regions without having to piece together separate trips themselves.

However, **the word VIP does not, by itself, define exactly which services are included**. Hotel category, transport, excursion type, and guiding should all be assessed from the published itinerary. Moreover, a 26-day trip does not mean that all 26 days are spent in the south or in Ushuaia.

## Sea journeys: Ushuaia as the final port

### 5 days among the fjords of Tierra del Fuego

The [5-day "Tierra del Fuego Fjords" cruise](/multi-country/tour/tierra-del-fuego-fjords/) sails **from Punta Arenas to Ushuaia**, traveling through the Strait of Magellan, islands, bays, and channels. The main experience is sailing along remote shores, observing nature, and approaching Patagonia's marine landscapes. The route ends in Ushuaia.

This tour suits people who want to discover the archipelago from the water. It is not equivalent to several days of land-based excursions in the city and national park. If you also dream of visiting the lakes or walking Tierra del Fuego's trails, allow extra time after the cruise finishes.

### 9 days: Chilean fjords and Patagonia

On the [9-day "Patagonia and Chilean Fjords" expedition cruise](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chilean-fjords/), the vessel travels **from Puerto Montt to Ushuaia** through Chilean fjords, national parks, glacial bays, and marine channels. Depending on actual conditions along the route, the program includes opportunities to see glaciers and visit natural sites by expedition boat.

This itinerary is longer than the 5-day cruise because it covers a more extensive section of Chile's coastline. Ushuaia remains the final destination. The list and order of marine areas, landing arrangements, and onboard conditions are more useful for comparing the cruises than the fact that both end in the same port.

### 6 days: from Ushuaia via Cape Horn to Antarctica

The [6-day "Antarctica Express" program](/multi-country/tour/antarctica-patagonia-express-air-cruise-6-days/) begins with boarding a vessel in Ushuaia. It then travels through the Beagle Channel, the Cape Horn area, and Drake Passage to Antarctic islands. The format combines a sea journey with a final flight.

The main attraction here is entering Antarctic waters and experiencing expedition geography, while Ushuaia is the port of departure. It would be the wrong choice if your main interest were exploring Tierra del Fuego itself in depth. Departure dates, flights, and conditions for the sea crossing should be checked against the offer for your selected departure: weather and expedition circumstances affect the program.

## A separate outing from Ushuaia: crabs and Puerto Almanza

Travelers already on Tierra del Fuego can choose a [one-day fishing and food excursion](/argentina/tour/ushuaia-fishing/). It starts in Ushuaia, goes to [Puerto Almanza](/argentina/place/puerto-almanza/), and includes a boat outing with local fishermen to king crab traps, followed by lunch. The product page gives the total duration as approximately 8 hours.

This trip **does not replace a full 12- or 16-day itinerary**: it focuses on one activity and may be an interesting addition to a stay in the city. The published terms specify English as the operating language, a November–March season, weather restrictions, and participation requirements. The program is not suitable for minors or people with reduced mobility; waterproof shoes are required. Check the specific product page for included services and possible changes.

## Which experiences should you choose around Ushuaia?

If you have free time, start with [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/). Forests, coastal areas, and [Lapataia Bay](/argentina/place/lapataia-bay/) let you experience the nature that draws so many travelers to Tierra del Fuego. There is an organized [national park excursion](/argentina/ushuaia/argentina-ushuaia-tierra-del-fuego-national-park/). It is a separate product and should not be assumed to be included in every cruise that calls at Ushuaia.

For marine landscapes, consider trips on the [Beagle Channel](/argentina/place/beagle-channel/). Seabirds are seen on the water and marine animals can be observed around the islands. To see penguins, the selection includes a [boat trip to Martillo Island](/argentina/ushuaia/martillo-island-penguin-boat-trip/) and a [walk with penguins](/argentina/ushuaia/ushuaia-walking-with-penguins/). These are **different ways to observe wildlife**: actual sightings, permission to land, and visiting conditions depend on the particular excursion and season.

For a more active day, consider the [Laguna Esmeralda hike](/argentina/ushuaia/laguna-esmeralda-hike-from-ushuaia/). For travelers who want to view mountains, forests, and water from above, a [helicopter flight over Ushuaia](/argentina/ushuaia/ushuaia-helicopter-flight/) is another option, weather permitting. Choose such experiences individually based on physical effort, available time, and the actual contents of your multi-day tour.

## How many days should you spend in Ushuaia?

For an initial introduction to the city and surrounding nature, allow **2–3 full days**, excluding complex flight connections: one for the national park, another for the Beagle Channel or islands, and one more for lakes, a walk, or rest. This is a planning guideline for a self-designed itinerary, not a promise that every tour already includes that many free days.

The [12-day "Ice, Sun and the End of the World" program](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/) includes 2 nights in Ushuaia, so your activity choices depend on its schedule. The [16-day tour](/argentina/tour/explore-argentina-16-days/) includes several distinct excursions around the city. If your sea voyage ends in Ushuaia, any extra stay must be arranged separately from the ship's program.

## When to travel: weather, sea, and seasons

Ushuaia has a cool, windy maritime climate. Even during the Southern Hemisphere summer, from December to February, the weather changes quickly, with sunny periods alternating with rain, wind, and cold spells. A waterproof jacket, several clothing layers, and shoes with good traction are useful on exposed decks and trails.

Most walks in the national park and excursions to the lakes are easier to plan around the long summer daylight hours. **Boat departures and wildlife viewing have their own seasonal patterns**: ship schedules, permitted landings, and excursion availability cannot automatically be assumed to be the same from one month to another. Winter in Ushuaia is attractive for snowy scenery and mountain activities, but it is a different type of trip from a summer cruise, with different conditions.

When choosing an itinerary, check the dates, the time buffer before boarding a ship, and potential weather delays. For expeditions, especially, avoid very short flight connections on your arrival or departure day. Compare the broader geography of these journeys in the [Argentina cruises and expeditions catalog](/interests/cruises-and-expeditions/tours/argentina/) and wildlife-viewing options among the country's [nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/).

## Frequently asked questions

### Which tours let you spend several days in Ushuaia?

Overland itineraries are usually better suited to this. The [12-day "Ice, Sun and the End of the World" tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/) includes 2 nights, while the [16-day program](/argentina/tour/explore-argentina-16-days/) features the national park, a boat trip, and an excursion to the lakes. Check day by day which activities are included and which may be added.

### Can I start a journey to Antarctica from Ushuaia?

Yes. The Ada Tours catalog includes a [6-day "Antarctica Express" program](/multi-country/tour/antarctica-patagonia-express-air-cruise-6-days/) departing from Ushuaia via the Beagle Channel and Cape Horn. Ushuaia is primarily the departure port on this itinerary. Actual dates, vessel, and conditions for a specific departure should be confirmed in the expedition offer.

### How do the 5- and 9-day cruises to Ushuaia differ?

The [5-day "Tierra del Fuego Fjords" cruise](/multi-country/tour/tierra-del-fuego-fjords/) departs Punta Arenas through the southern channels. The [9-day cruise](/multi-country/tour/patagonia-chilean-fjords/) begins much farther north, in Puerto Montt, and covers a longer stretch of Chilean Patagonia. Both end in Ushuaia, but the routes by sea are different.

### Where can I see penguins around Ushuaia?

Separate excursion programs feature [Martillo Island](/argentina/place/martillo-island/). There are options for [viewing from a boat](/argentina/ushuaia/martillo-island-penguin-boat-trip/) and [walking with penguins](/argentina/ushuaia/ushuaia-walking-with-penguins/). Not every excursion allows a landing. Availability depends on season, local rules, and the chosen product.

### Which tour should I choose for Lake Fagnano and Lake Escondido?

Look for tours where an off-road excursion is listed on a separate day, such as the [16-day Argentina itinerary](/argentina/tour/explore-argentina-16-days/) or the [13-day Argentina and Chile journey](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/). A ship's visit to Ushuaia does not, by itself, include the lakes.

### Can crab fishing be added to a longer journey?

Our selection includes a [one-day excursion from Ushuaia to Puerto Almanza](/argentina/tour/ushuaia-fishing/). It may be considered as a separate activity when you have a free day, but whether it fits the dates and itinerary of the main tour must be agreed separately. This outing has its own restrictions regarding season, age, participants' mobility, and weather.
